problem: Mainstream robotics simulators such as Gazebo have no maintained native event-camera model, so researchers must use cumbersome offline converters (ESIM/v2e). As a result there is no simulation-ready, end-to-end framework for learning closed-loop event-based robot policies for navigation and manipulation, nor direct comparisons with RGB policies.
motivation: Event cameras offer microsecond latency, high dynamic range and no motion blur, which suits fast-moving or challenging robotic scenes. Evaluating event-driven policies at scale requires easy in-simulator event generation. The paper embeds v2e in ROS2/Gazebo and trains transformer policies by behavior cloning to compare event, RGB and fused inputs.
key_idea: Embed a v2e event emulator as a ROS2 node in Gazebo and train a compact early-fusion ViT policy on RGB plus ON/OFF event frames for object-following navigation and pre-grasp pose prediction.
insight: Early fusion of RGB and event frames beats either modality alone on both tasks. For example, ERPArm single-object success is 51.7% for RGB+Event versus 28.4% for RGB and 26.9% for Event. Event-only has the lowest latency (3.2 ms vs 5.7 ms RGB and 7.8 ms fused) but the lowest accuracy, so events complement RGB rather than replace it. The evidence is small-scale (15 episodes per condition, simulation only, no blur/lighting stress test), so the gains should be read cautiously.
method: v2e ROS2 emulator: subscribes to /camera/image_raw, resizes and converts to grayscale, feeds v2ecore EventEmulator, publishes /dvs/events; tunable thresholds (pos/neg 0.3, sigma 0.09, cutoff 15 Hz, downsample 0.5, 3x3 blur); tested on ROS2 Humble with Gazebo Classic
Observation encoding: RGB image plus event frame accumulated over Δt into ON and OFF count channels, giving a 5-channel early-fused input

ERP transformer backbone: ViT-style, 16x16 patches projected to 64-d (1,600 tokens), class token, sinusoidal positional encoding, one 4-head self-attention layer plus 256-unit FFN, LayerNorm, dropout 0.1
ERPNav head: MLP outputs linear-x and angular-z velocity (Twist), trained with MSE behavior cloning against a YOLOv8+PID expert
ERPArm head: deeper MLP regresses a 6-DoF pre-grasp end-effector pose from a single wrist-camera observation, trained with Smooth L1 loss against a YOLOv8+MoveIt expert

Expert datasets: ERPNav has 70 episodes (~65 min, 32,033 action labels) on a 4-wheel differential-drive robot; ERPArm has 35 episodes (~70 min, 18,417 waypoints) on UR5 with Robotiq 2F-85 and a conveyor belt
Ablation variants: RGB-only, Event-only and RGB+Event trained with identical hyperparameters (Adam, 10 epochs, batch 32, early stopping)

setting.backbone: Compact ViT-style transformer encoder (single layer), trained from scratch; three variants RGB / Event / RGB+Event
setting.training_data: Simulated expert demonstrations in Gazebo: ERPNav 70 episodes / 32,033 samples; ERPArm 35 episodes / 18,417 waypoints
setting.observation: RGB (640x640) plus v2e-synthesized ON/OFF event frames; wrist-mounted camera for the arm
setting.action_space: Continuous linear/angular velocity (cmd_vel) for the mobile robot; 6-DoF end-effector pre-grasp pose for the UR5
setting.privileged: none at test time (YOLO expert only used to generate training demonstrations)

results: RGB+Event early fusion is best on both tasks in simulation. For navigation it reaches 93.3% success vs 86.7% for RGB and 73.3% for Event, with centroid error of 106.7 px vs 129.7 px for RGB. For grasping it reaches 51.7% single-object success (vs 28.4% RGB) and 31.8% multi-object (vs 26.1% RGB), at higher latency (7.8 ms vs 5.7 ms RGB and 3.2 ms Event).
limitations: Simulation only with synthetic v2e events; no real event camera or sim-to-real evaluation, and no motion-blur or lighting stress tests despite the claims
Small evaluation (15 episodes per condition), a single simple cube target, tiny one-layer transformer, no comparison against other published methods
Arm policy predicts a pre-grasp pose from a single frame, and the fused variant has higher latency than RGB
